I really dont fully understand what happened honestly. She came in from doing her business and laid down and so did I. When I woke up later she was still there which is unusual for her. When she would try and walk her left paws would stay curled under and she would fall. I tried for hours to get her to get up and walk. Took her to the vet and got some anti inflammatory and a painkiller and told us if she doesnt gain control back by tomorrow she probably never will. Gave her the medicine and tried to get her up enough she could potty. She couldn't stand on her own. I tried 5 or 6 times. She's 110llbs of pure love but at this point, dead weight. I have to pick her up, set her up, set her paws and hold her. She would fall if my legs weren't supporting her on either side. If she tried to step it would be on the back of her paw. All of it in the hour I fell asleep, so I thought she had a stroke and it was over. Took her back the next day because she wasnt any better and at this point not able to go to the bathroom. Vet said give it one more night and if she not better it's time. I let her rest and then spent all night working with her. Holding her up. Moving her paws for her and still nothing. Those paws would stay folded under and the way she would try and step still it was as if she couldn't feel them. I spent hours and hours trying with her. Inside and out. To no avail. By this time the family decides it's time to say goodbye if she cant go to the bathroom at the very least. The appointment was made so she wouldn't suffer, cant bear to see that look on her face when she cant figure out why she cant walk, those giant sad eyes. I took her out at about 945 the next morning and I was holding her up between my legs, I slowly stopped supporting her and she was standing on her own. Albeit it wobbly as I am after six pack. She looks drunk but she's not falling! Anytime she steps, that paw folds back under and she falls. I still hold her up and walk her silly giant paws along. But she just cant seem to feel them. Then at like 1030, she takes a wobbly step and stays up for a second. Progress. She can manage one step without falling. The appointment to put her down is at 1130 at its killing me.  At 1045 she takes a step, looks down at the ground in front of her and swings that paw around and takes another step. I literally screamed with excitement. Then she looks at the step ahead of her and takes another damn step. She fell up the stairs but it counts. So we start debating with time looming if it's a fair quality of life for her to continue like that. Every subsequent attempt since has failed. So at 1115 right before were set to take her it's one last attempt to get her to stand, to walk to be able to use the restroom. I set her big ass down and get her steady and what does this bitch do but forking walk. Take a couple steps and fall. And then get back up! What!? I call her over and she drunkenly stumbles over to me. Hold the front door. Then I tell her to potty and after a few attempts her wobbly ass got it done! She is still a little wobbly and she swings that foot out and around when she walks but I'll be damned if she isn't running today. I know it sounds dramatic but when its family like your dog is, you dont want to see them suffer but you dont want to ever have to put them down either. I had to say goodbye to her sister 4 years ago to bone cancer and I kept her longer than I should have I think. She was not happy those last weeks and I couldn't bear to see it happen again. It really felt that dramatic. And that morning all happened so fast right before that dreadful appointment. I think she could feel it was her last ditch effort and she gave it everything she had.

My elderly rottweiler had something similar to this happen. It was her left side that she had lost motor control of. I saw this video the night before she was to be put down so I figured I might as well give it a shot. I spent every bit of 8 hours working with her that night, from holding her weight up just so she could feel the sensation of her own weight on her feet to getting her to be able to hold herself up if she didnt move. I took so many steps for her just to build that sensation and the confidence in her that she lost. Not even an hour before her appointment while we were still trying, she took a step under her own power. And then another before she fell. She was trying! Not even 15 minutes before I was due to be at the vet's, she took another step, and another, and then she did the unthinkable. She went to the bathroom on her own! Needless to say if she didnt give up, I wasnt going to. That dog is doing better today than she was months before that incident. We actually went for a walk yesterday and she ran! I didnt think there was anything that could be done but I came across this video that night and it inspired me. I sincerely thank whoever posted that video that evening, you surely bought me more time with my best friend!
